entries.name: Bent Over Barbell Row
entries.reason: Redrawn on 9 October 2026 at the owner's request, because the earlier drawing was against this text: the torso was held about 40 degrees above level. Source-bound side-view draft: hinged over soft knees with a straight back until the trunk is almost level, the bar hanging under the shoulders on straight arms; the trunk and legs do not move while the bar is pulled up and back to the body with the elbows leading, a squeeze, and a slower lowering to a full hang. The bar is seen end-on. Not drawn: the overhand grip.
entries.summary: Hinged forward with a straight back until the torso is almost level, pull the bar from a full hang up to the body with the torso still, squeeze, then lower slowly.

frames.caption: Hold a barbell with an overhand grip, bend the knees slightly and hinge forward with the back straight until the torso is almost level with the floor and the bar hangs under the shoulders.
Keeping the torso still and the elbows close to the body, pull the bar up to the body.
Squeeze the back. Lead with the elbows.
Lower the bar slowly to a full hang.
Back straight, torso still.

entries.name: Bent Over One-Arm Long Bar Row
entries.reason: Redrawn on 9 October 2026 at the owner's request, because the earlier drawing was against this text: no bar or plates were drawn. Source-bound side-view draft: one end of the bar is braced on the floor behind the athlete and the loaded end is in front; hinged over slightly bent knees, the near hand grips the shaft just behind the plates and the free hand rests on the thigh above the knee. The trunk does not move while the bar swings up about its braced end until the plates reach the lower chest, a squeeze, and a slower lowering that stops short of the floor. One arm is shown; the last caption carries the change of arms.
entries.summary: Hinged beside a bar braced at its far end, one hand just behind the plates and the other on the knee, pull the bar up until the plates reach the lower chest, squeeze, lower slowly, then change arms.

frames.caption: Load one end of a barbell and brace the other end in a corner, then hinge forward with the knees slightly bent, grip the bar just behind the plates with one hand and rest the other hand on the knee.
Keeping the torso still and the elbow in, pull the bar straight up until the plates reach the lower chest.
Squeeze. Elbow close to the body.
Lower slowly without letting the plates rest on the floor.
Complete the repetitions, then change arms.

entries.name: Bent Over Two-Dumbbell Row
entries.reason: Own drawn frames authored for this repository: the bent-over family body with a dumbbell in each hand rowing together on the shared ladder. Standard two-dumbbell setup chosen from the template; listed in the daily review. The flat back is the fix that was needed: the spine ran 32.0 degrees above horizontal, which reads as a good morning rather than a row, and now runs 6.0. The head sits 9.00 along the spine from the neck and 0.00 off the spine line, so "head in line with the trunk" was already true and is preserved rather than re-claimed. The dumbbells hang straight down from the new shoulder and the pull brings them to the ribs. The elbow is re-solved on the shoulder circle per frame, so the upper arm (12.5) and forearm (12.0) hold their length by construction. Draft preview pending qualified technique review.
entries.summary: Six drawn positions of a bent-over two-dumbbell row, seen from the side.

frames.caption: Flat back, dumbbells hanging straight under the shoulders.
Pull the elbows back past the ribs.
Dumbbells at the ribs, back still flat.
Hold at the ribs with the trunk level.
Lower the dumbbells back under control.
Back to a full hang with the spine level.

entries.name: Bent Over Two-Dumbbell Row With Palms In
entries.reason: Own drawn frames authored for this repository: the two-dumbbell bent-over row with the bells drawn standing VERTICAL so the palms-in grip is visible; the palms stay in through the pull. Standard palms-in setup chosen from the template; listed in the daily review. The flat back is the fix that was needed: the spine ran 32.0 degrees above horizontal and now runs 6.0. The palms-in grip keeps the same flat trunk and takes a shorter, tighter pull that stops nearer the body, which is what separates it from the base on the sheet. The head sits 9.00 along the spine from the neck and 0.00 off the spine line, so "head in line with the trunk" was already true and is preserved rather than re-claimed. The dumbbells hang straight down from the new shoulder and the pull brings them to the ribs. The elbow is re-solved on the shoulder circle per frame, so the upper arm (12.5) and forearm (12.0) hold their length by construction. Draft preview pending qualified technique review.
entries.summary: Six drawn positions of a bent-over two-dumbbell row with palms in, seen from the side.

frames.caption: Flat back, palms turned in, dumbbells hanging.
Draw the elbows back close to the ribs.
Dumbbells tight to the body, spine still level.
Hold the squeeze with the trunk flat.
Lower the dumbbells back under control.
Back to a full hang with the spine level.

entries.name: Barbell Row
entries.reason: Source-bound draft, drawn from a 3D model turned 28 degrees so the grip just outside the legs, the soft knees, the bar hanging plumb beneath the shoulders in straight arms, the elbows driving behind the trunk as the bar rows to the lower ribs, and the unchanging torso angle all read clearly.
entries.summary: Hinged over soft knees with the bar hanging beneath the shoulders just outside the legs, drive the elbows back to row toward the lower ribs, then lower to long arms without changing the torso angle.

frames.caption: Hold the bar just outside the legs, soften the knees, and hinge until the bar hangs beneath the shoulders with the trunk braced and the neck long.
Drive the elbows back to row the bar toward the lower ribs.
Drive the elbows behind you and hold one torso angle.
Lower to long arms without changing the torso angle.
Brace the hinge before the pull and hold one torso angle for the set.

entries.name: One-Arm Kettlebell Row
entries.reason: Source-bound draft, drawn from a 3D model turned 28 degrees so the staggered stance, the square hips and long torso, the downward scapular reach at the bottom with the kettlebell hanging plumb beneath the working shoulder, and the pull toward the back pocket with the elbow past the ribs all read clearly.
entries.summary: In a staggered stance with a long, square torso and the kettlebell hanging beneath one shoulder, row the bell toward the back pocket by driving the elbow past the ribs, then lower until the shoulder blade reaches naturally.

frames.caption: Take a staggered stance, hinge until the torso is long and stable, and let the kettlebell hang beneath one shoulder.
Row the bell toward the back pocket by driving the elbow past the ribs while the hips stay square to the floor.
Set a long, square torso and drive the elbow toward the back pocket.
Lower until the shoulder blade reaches naturally.
Keep the hips square to the floor and reach the shoulder blade at the bottom.

entries.name: Reverse Grip Bent-Over Rows
entries.reason: Source-bound draft, drawn from a 3D model turned 28 degrees with a close-up of the near hand showing the closed underhand grip wrapped around the bar: hinged over soft knees with the hands just outside the thighs, pulling the elbows back to row the bar to the lower ribs, holding the top, and lowering to long arms without changing the hinge.
entries.summary: Hinged over soft knees with an underhand grip just outside the thighs, row the bar toward the lower ribs, hold the top long enough for the shoulder blades to finish, then lower to long arms without changing the hinge.

frames.caption: Take an underhand grip just outside the thighs, soften the knees, and hinge until the bar hangs below the shoulders with the torso braced.
Pull the elbows back and row the bar toward the lower ribs.
Hold the top long enough to feel the shoulder blades finish.
Lower to long arms without changing the hinge.
Brace the hinge before the pull, touch the lower ribs, and own the way down.

entries.name: Two-Arm Kettlebell Row
entries.reason: Source-bound draft, drawn from a 3D model turned 28 degrees so both kettlebells beneath the shoulders over the feet, the hips pushed back over slightly bent knees, the straight back, and both bells rowing together toward the stomach before lowering under control to straight arms all read clearly.
entries.summary: Standing over two kettlebells with the knees slightly bent, hips back, and back straight, pull both kettlebells toward the stomach together, then lower them under control until the arms are straight.

frames.caption: Stand over two kettlebells, bend the knees slightly, push the hips back and take a handle in each hand with the back straight.
Pull both kettlebells toward the stomach, drawing the shoulder blades together.
Pull the elbows toward the hips with the back straight.
Lower them under control until the arms are straight.
Hips back, back straight, and lower under control.

entries.name: T-Bar Row
entries.reason: Source-bound draft, drawn from a 3D model turned 28 degrees so the feet straddling the anchored landmine bar, the rear pivot on the floor, the 45-degree hinge, the neutral grip on the handle, the plates floating off the floor at full stretch, and the pull to the chest with elbows driven up and back all read clearly.
entries.summary: Straddling an anchored bar in a 45-degree hinge with a neutral grip on the handle, pull the plates to your chest by driving the elbows up and back, then lower to a full stretch with the plates floating off the floor.

frames.caption: Straddle the bar, hinge to about 45 degrees, and take the handle with a neutral grip with the plates floating off the floor.
Pull the plates to your chest, driving the elbows up and back.
Pull with the elbows to the chest while holding your hinge angle.
Let the bar stretch your lats at the bottom of the rep with the plates floating.
Lock your hinge angle and defend it all set.

entries.name: Alternating Kettlebell Row
entries.reason: Source-bound draft, drawn from a 3D model turned 28 degrees so both kettlebells resting on the floor beneath the shoulders, the flat hinged back, one kettlebell rowing to the lower ribs while the other stays on the floor in a straight arm, and the alternating repetition on the other side all read clearly.
entries.summary: Standing over two kettlebells on the floor with the knees slightly bent, hips back, and back flat, row one kettlebell toward the lower ribs while the other stays on the floor, lower under control, then row the other side.

frames.caption: Stand over two kettlebells, bend the knees slightly, push the hips back and take a handle in each hand with the back flat.
Pull one kettlebell toward the lower ribs, drawing that shoulder blade back, while the other hand holds its kettlebell on the floor.
Lower it under control to the floor while keeping the chest square to the floor.
Row the other side toward the lower ribs while the first kettlebell stays on the floor.
Lower it under control to the floor with the hips back and the back flat.
